sites_https_justification: All project sites are served over HTTPS only: the repository (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder), the pkgdown site on GitLab Pages (https://punycoder-a165b3.gitlab.io) and the CRAN page (https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=punycoder).
description_good_justification: DESCRIPTION and README provide a clear, succinct description of what punycoder does: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/README.md
interact_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to interact with and contribute to the project: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) states the requirements for acceptable contributions: tests for every user-visible change, stable exported signatures unless a break is planned, preserved R-facing error prefixes, and small reviewable patches. It names the pre-commit pre-push hook, which runs lintr and R CMD check --as-cran failing on any warning, as what gates a merge.
license_location_justification: LICENSE is at the repository top level: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/LICENSE
floss_license_osi_justification: MIT is an OSI-approved open source license: https://opensource.org/license/mit
documentation_basics_justification: The pkgdown site https://punycoder-a165b3.gitlab.io carries the README (installation and use), the introduction vignette and the function reference. The sources are README.md and vignettes/ in the repository (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/tree/main/vignettes).
documentation_interface_justification: Every exported function is documented with roxygen2. The reference is published at https://punycoder-a165b3.gitlab.io/reference/ and rendered by CRAN at https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=punycoder .
repo_public_justification: Public GitLab repository: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder. The GitHub repository is a read-only mirror.
repo_track_justification: All changes are tracked in git: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/commits/main
repo_interim_justification: Interim development commits are publicly available on GitLab between releases: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/commits/main
repo_distributed_justification: Uses git, a distributed version control system: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder
version_unique_justification: Each release carries a unique version (DESCRIPTION Version; CRAN enforces uniqueness): https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=punycoder
version_semver_justification: Uses semantic-style x.y.z versioning; release tags visible at https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/tags
version_tags_justification: Releases are tagged in git (vX.Y.Z) and distributed through CRAN: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/tags
release_notes_justification: NEWS.md documents user-facing changes for each release: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/NEWS.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerabilities have been fixed to date; NEWS.md records all changes: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/NEWS.md
report_tracker_justification: GitLab work items serve as the public issue tracker: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/work_items
report_process_justification: Users submit bug reports through the GitLab issue tracker, which offers a Bug issue template (.gitlab/issue_templates/Bug.md): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/work_items
report_responses_justification: Maintainer responds to issue reports on the tracker: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/work_items
enhancement_responses_justification: Maintainer responds to enhancement requests on the tracker, which offers a Feature issue template (.gitlab/issue_templates/Feature.md): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/work_items
report_archive_justification: GitLab Issues provide a publicly available, searchable archive of reports and responses: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/work_items/?state=all
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: The vulnerability-reporting process is published in the security policy: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md . Reports go to the maintainer by email, with a confidential GitLab issue as a documented alternative.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md) documents two confidential channels: email to the maintainer, and a confidential GitLab issue (open a new item at https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/work_items and tick 'This issue is confidential'), visible only to project maintainers. The GitHub repository is a read-only mirror with private vulnerability reporting turned off.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging reports within 7 days and coordinating a fix and disclosure: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md
build_justification: Builds with the standard R toolchain (R CMD build / INSTALL, devtools) plus the configure script that detects libidn2: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/configure
build_common_tools_justification: Uses the standard, widely available R build tooling plus a POSIX configure script.
build_floss_tools_justification: R, GCC/Clang, and the entire build toolchain are free/open source software: https://www.r-project.org/
test_invocation_justification: Tests run via devtools::test() and as part of R CMD check.
test_most_justification: covr measures coverage in the `coverage` CI job on every push to main and reports it through GitLab's native coverage reporting; the latest main pipeline (2026-09-24) measured 97.82% line coverage: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/pipelines
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires tests for every user-visible change: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
tests_are_added_justification: New functionality ships with tests, enforced in review.
tests_documented_added_justification: The test-addition policy is documented in CONTRIBUTING.md: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
warnings_justification: lintr and R CMD check surface warnings in the pre-push verification chain and in the `lint` and `check` CI jobs on every push to main: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
warnings_fixed_justification: Warnings are fixed before merge: the verification chain and the `check` CI job fail on any R CMD check warning, and `lint` fails on any lint.
warnings_strict_justification: The `lint` CI job sets LINTR_ERROR_ON_LINT=true so any lint fails, and `check` runs rcmdcheck with error_on = "warning"; the pre-push verification chain applies the same rules to R CMD check --as-cran: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer applies secure design principles; punycoder defensively handles untrusted Punycode/IDNA input through its C/C++ codec core, enforcing length limits, valid UTF-8, and label-structure rules.
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer knows the common C/C++ memory-safety and IDNA parsing pitfalls (buffer overflows, integer overflows, invalid UTF-8, homograph attacks). The C++ codec core validates UTF-8 and enforces label and DNS length limits on untrusted input.
crypto_password_storage_justification: punycoder stores no passwords or credentials.
crypto_random_justification: punycoder does not generate security-sensitive random values.
crypto_used_network_justification: punycoder is a string/IDNA library and does not itself make network connections.
crypto_tls12_justification: punycoder does not establish network connections.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: punycoder does not establish network connections.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: punycoder does not establish network connections.
delivery_mitm_justification: Distributed via CRAN and GitLab over HTTPS; CRAN publishes per-package checksums: https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=punycoder
delivery_unsigned_justification: All distribution downloads are served over HTTPS (CRAN and GitLab): https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=punycoder
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No outstanding known vulnerabilities; tracker at https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/work_items
static_analysis_justification: lintr (a full-package lint using the goodpractice-aligned linter set in .lintr) and R CMD check run in the pre-push verification chain and in the `lint` and `check` CI jobs on every push to main: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: lintr and R CMD check find defects but are not vulnerability scanners, and no vulnerability-focused analyzer (such as a C/C++ SAST tool) is run over the codec core in src/. The osv-audit job checks dependencies against OSV weekly, but that is SCA, not static analysis of punycoder's own code: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
static_analysis_fixed_justification: The verification chain fails on any lintr finding or R CMD check warning, so static-analysis findings are fixed before merge.
static_analysis_often_justification: lintr runs on every push: the verification chain is a pre-push hook, and the `lint` CI job runs again on every push to main: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
dynamic_analysis_justification: No dynamic analysis tool is run routinely. A manual `sanitizers` CI job is configured to run R CMD check inside R-hub's clang-ASAN/UBSAN and valgrind container images (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml), but it has not been run since the project moved to GitLab CI.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: punycoder ships C/C++ in src/ (the RFC 3492 codec and the UTS #46 normalizer), but no memory-safety tool is run over it routinely. The manual `sanitizers` CI job (clang-ASAN/UBSAN and valgrind) is configured but has not yet been run on GitLab: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The testthat suite's expectations (expect_*) are assertions checked at runtime on every run of the verification chain and the `check` CI job: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/tree/main/tests/testthat
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis is run (see dynamic_analysis), so there are no findings to fix.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: The GitLab CI pipeline (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/pipelines) runs lint, README sync, NEWS/version, citation-version, R CMD check and coverage on every push to main (configuration: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml ). Branch pushes and merge requests start no pipeline; the same verification chain runs as a pre-push hook on every branch before it leaves a contributor's machine.
discussion_justification: GitLab Issues provide a public forum for project discussion: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/work_items
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials are committed. A gitleaks scan of the full git history (271 commits, 2026-09-26) found only two false positives: the fixed 'Generator token' UUID that Rcpp::compileAttributes() writes into R/RcppExports.R and src/RcppExports.cpp: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder
english_justification: Documentation and issue-tracker interaction are conducted in English (Language: en-US): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/README.md
hardening_justification: Hardening mechanisms (e.g. HTTP security headers) apply to web applications; punycoder is an R library.
sites_password_security_justification: Project sites (GitLab, CRAN) manage their own authentication; punycoder operates no site with user passwords.
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: recent CRAN releases, frequent commits, and responsive issue handling: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/commits/main
